For similar polygons, the ratios of lengths of the corresponding sides should be the same.

- Let's check for this in option I:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}} & =\frac{4}{16}=\frac{1}{4}, \\ \frac{BC}{{B}^{′}{C}^{′}} & =\frac{6}{24}=\frac{1}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, option I does give possible values of ${A}^{′}{B}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}{C}^{′}.$

- For option II, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}} & =\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{5}, \\ \frac{BC}{{B}^{′}{C}^{′}} & =\frac{6}{30}=\frac{1}{5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, option II does give possible values of ${A}^{′}{B}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}{C}^{′}.$

- For option III, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}} & =\frac{4}{32}=\frac{1}{8}, \\ \frac{BC}{{B}^{′}{C}^{′}} & =\frac{6}{42}=\frac{1}{7}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, option III does not give possible values of ${A}^{′}{B}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}{C}^{′}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
